accepted.s:
With reference to Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS), consider the following statements:
1. CSS are designed by the Centre for implementation in areas falling under State subjects.
2. General States ordinarily bear 40 per cent of the cost of a CSS.
3. Special Category and Himalayan States ordinarily follow a 90:10 Centre-State sharing pattern.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CSS are Centre-designed schemes implemented in State or Concurrent subjects. The usual sharing pattern is 60:40 for general States and 90:10 for Special Category or Himalayan States.
accepted.tq: Combine the subject classification with the two funding ratios and identify the complete set.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: The allocation for Centrally Sponsored Schemes in Andhra Pradesh in 2021-22 was approximately:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s CSS allocation in 2021-22 was Rs. 17,289 crore.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact year-linked allocation rather than confusing it with other grants-in-aid figures.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: The amount of other grants-in-aid from the Government of India, including CSS but excluding Finance Commission and externally aided project assistance, was Rs. 25,035 crore for Andhra Pradesh in:
accepted.x: Other grants-in-aid including CSS amounted to Rs. 25,035 crore in 2023-24. The corresponding figures were Rs. 22,953 crore in 2022-23, Rs. 17,036 crore in 2024-25 RE and Rs. 21,711 crore in 2025-26 RE.
accepted.tq: Match the exact amount with its financial year and distinguish it from adjacent annual figures.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: SNA-SPARSH is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: A mechanism for converting revenue-deficit grants into loans
A system for calculating the State’s inter-se tax devolution share
A formula for sharing Polavaram construction expenditure between two States
Just-in-time release of CSS funds through State IFMIS, RBI e-Kuber and PFMS
accepted.x: SNA-SPARSH enables just-in-time release of CSS funds from the Centre and State Consolidated Funds through State IFMIS, RBI e-Kuber and PFMS.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational function of the financial management system rather than its institutional channels alone.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: SNA-SPARSH has been implemented across:
o: 28 States and 2 Union Territories covering 66 notified CSS
30 States and 3 Union Territories covering 60 notified CSS
All States and all Union Territories covering every CSS
28 States and 3 Union Territories covering 66 notified CSS
accepted.x: SNA-SPARSH operates in all 28 States and 3 Union Territories across 66 notified Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
accepted.tq: Test the precise combination of geographical coverage and scheme count.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: What was the principal effect of shifting from a ‘credit-push’ to a ‘debit-pull’ mechanism in CSS fund management?
o: Idle float increased from Rs. 0.4 lakh crore to Rs. 1.67 lakh crore
CSS funding changed from 60:40 to 90:10 for all States
Idle float declined from Rs. 1.67 lakh crore to Rs. 0.4 lakh crore
State contributions were eliminated from CSS
accepted.x: The debit-pull system reduced idle float from Rs. 1.67 lakh crore to Rs. 0.4 lakh crore by enabling funds to be drawn when required.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of change and compare the two exact numerical values.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: The new five-year appraisal cycle for Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes is to begin from:
accepted.x: The new five-year CSS and Central Sector Scheme appraisal cycle begins on 1 April 2026 and is aligned with the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Recall the commencement date attached to the appraisal-cycle reform.
accepted.sec: Centrally sponsored schemes in AP - AP's rank, fund-sharing, SNA-SPARSH

accepted.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission has favoured linking Centrally Sponsored Schemes primarily to:
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission has sought to link CSS with measurable outcomes.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy objective most directly associated with performance-linked scheme appraisal.

accepted.s: During the Plan era, State Plans were financed through which combination?
o: Only tax devolution and Finance Commission grants
State’s own resources and Normal Central Assistance
Central Sector Scheme grants and small savings alone
accepted.x: State Plans were financed through the State’s own resources together with Normal Central Assistance allocated under the Gadgil or Gadgil-Mukherjee formula.
accepted.tq: Distinguish historical Plan financing from the later tax-devolution framework.
accepted.sec: Financing of AP Plans - central assistance vs State's own resources (historical)

accepted.s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, the loan-grant composition of Normal Central Assistance for general category States was:
accepted.x: For general category States, Normal Central Assistance consisted of loans and grants in a 70:30 ratio. For Special Category States, the ratio was 10:90.
accepted.tq: Separate the historical loan-grant ratio from the CSS Centre-State sharing ratio.
accepted.sec: Financing of AP Plans - central assistance vs State's own resources (historical)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change associated with the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
o: The Plan and non-Plan distinction was restored in the 2017-18 Budget
Plan grants were increased to approximately 10 per cent of the divisible pool
Transfers shifted from Plan grants to tax devolution and State Plan grants were discontinued
Normal Central Assistance replaced tax devolution
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission shifted the emphasis from Plan grants to tax devolution, and State Plan grants of about 3 per cent of the divisible pool were discontinued.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional transition to reject the reversed or exaggerated alternatives.
accepted.sec: Financing of AP Plans - central assistance vs State's own resources (historical)

accepted.s: In 2022-23, the Finance Commission total transfers to Andhra Pradesh amounted to:
accepted.x: The Finance Commission total for Andhra Pradesh in 2022-23 was Rs. 51,351 crore. It comprised Rs. 38,177 crore in tax devolution and Rs. 13,174 crore in Finance Commission grants.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Finance Commission total from its tax-devolution component and total central transfers.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the Finance Commission total for Andhra Pradesh with the year?
accepted.x: The Finance Commission total was Rs. 55,352 crore in 2023-24 and Rs. 57,002 crore in 2024-25 RE.
accepted.tq: Match the annual total with the correct year while rejecting nearby figures from the same table.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s Finance Commission grants:
1. Finance Commission grants were Rs. 13,174 crore in 2022-23.
2. Finance Commission grants were Rs. 9,641 crore in 2023-24.
3. Finance Commission grants were estimated at Rs. 4,922 crore in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The decline reflects the tapering of the post-bifurcation revenue-deficit grant.
accepted.tq: Verify each year-specific entry in the same table before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s: For 2025-26 RE, which pair is correctly matched for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Total central transfers — Rs. 89,157 crore; Finance Commission line — Rs. 57,002 crore
Total central transfers — Rs. 1,04,493 crore; Finance Commission line — Rs. 62,188 crore
Total central transfers — Rs. 62,188 crore; Finance Commission line — Rs. 1,04,493 crore
Total central transfers — Rs. 81,563 crore; Finance Commission line — Rs. 51,351 crore
accepted.x: For 2025-26 RE, total central transfers were Rs. 1,04,493 crore and the Finance Commission line was Rs. 62,188 crore, the largest component.
accepted.tq: Match two related aggregates simultaneously to prevent confusing a component with the total.

accepted.s: The post-bifurcation revenue-deficit grant to Andhra Pradesh has been tapering off. Which amount was included in the SAM package as an RD grant?
accepted.x: The Special Assistance Measure package included an RD grant of Rs. 3,979 crore within the overall package of Rs. 24,350 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the component amount from the overall package amount and other grant figures.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the constitutional provision with its subject in relation to transfers to States?
o: Article 282 — statutory Finance Commission grants only
accepted.x: Article 270 deals with tax devolution. Article 275 provides statutory grants, including revenue-deficit, local-body and disaster-related grants; Article 282 concerns discretionary grants; and Article 280(3)(bb),(c) relates to local-body support.
accepted.tq: Use constitutional-article discrimination and reject swapped functions.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 275 grants are statutory grants charged on the Consolidated Fund.
2. Article 282 is associated with discretionary grants.
3. Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) relate to support for local bodies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Article 275 provides statutory grants, Article 282 concerns discretionary grants, and Article 280(3)(bb),(c) includes local-body-related functions.
accepted.tq: Test several constitutional provisions together, with each statement using a precise institutional function.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s: Which of the following represents the change in the States’ share in the divisible pool across the Fourteenth, Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions?
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission raised the share from 32 per cent to 42 per cent; the Fifteenth Finance Commission fixed it at 41 per cent, and the Sixteenth retained 41 per cent.
accepted.tq: Track the sequential percentage changes and distinguish the initial pre-Fourteenth figure from the Commission recommendations.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s: The reduction from 42 per cent under the Fourteenth Finance Commission to 41 per cent under the Fifteenth Finance Commission was associated with:
o: The change relating to Jammu and Kashmir
The discontinuation of Central Sector Schemes
accepted.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission’s 41 per cent share reflected the change relating to Jammu and Kashmir.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific institutional reason behind a one-percentage-point change.
accepted.sec: Finance Commission transfers to AP - devolution, revenue-deficit, local body and disaster grants

accepted.s: Who chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose award period is 2026-31?
accepted.x: Arvind Panagariya chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose award period is 2026-31.
accepted.tq: Test the chairperson associated with the specified Finance Commission period.

accepted.s: The divisible pool of the Centre’s gross tax revenue is approximately what proportion after excluding cesses and surcharges?
accepted.x: The divisible pool is approximately 81 per cent of the Centre’s gross tax revenue because cesses and surcharges are excluded.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the divisible pool from gross tax revenue by applying the stated exclusion.

accepted.s: An amount of Rs. 1,200 crore was cited as assistance for Andhra Pradesh in connection with:
accepted.x: Rs. 1,200 crore was cited as a disaster-related assistance amount for Cyclone Titli.
accepted.tq: Match the disaster event with its specific assistance amount.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Centrally Sponsored Schemes — State or Concurrent subjects
Central Sector Schemes — 100 per cent funded by the Centre
Centrally Sponsored Schemes — implemented and wholly funded by a Central Ministry
Central Sector Schemes — Union List subjects
accepted.x: Centrally Sponsored Schemes concern State or Concurrent subjects and are jointly funded by the Centre and States. Central Sector Schemes are 100 per cent Centre-funded and run by Central Ministries.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that wrongly transfers the funding and implementation features of Central Sector Schemes to CSS.
accepted.sec: Central sector vs centrally sponsored schemes - funding pattern

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: PM-KISAN and Ayushman Bharat are listed as Central Sector Schemes, whereas NHM and ICDS are Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
accepted.tq: Separate scheme examples by funding architecture rather than by their social-sector purpose.
accepted.sec: Central sector vs centrally sponsored schemes - funding pattern

accepted.s: According to the Budget 2026-27 comparison, Central Sector Schemes and Centrally Sponsored Schemes accounted for approximately what shares of Union spending, respectively?
accepted.x: Central Sector Schemes accounted for 17 per cent of Union spending, while Centrally Sponsored Schemes accounted for 8 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the categories in the stated order and avoid reversing the two percentages.
accepted.sec: Central sector vs centrally sponsored schemes - funding pattern

accepted.s: Under the funding pattern stated for MGNREGA, the wage component was shared between the Centre and States in the ratio of:
accepted.x: MGNREGA followed a 90:10 pattern in wage terms. Its replacement by the VB-G RAM G Act is associated with a 60:40 pattern for most States, increasing State contributions.
accepted.tq: Compare the earlier wage-sharing ratio with the later replacement framework.
accepted.sec: Central sector vs centrally sponsored schemes - funding pattern

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the financial responsibility for Polavaram as a national project?
o: The Centre is to fund the project, with an estimated cost cited as Rs. 55,548 crore
The Centre bears only 10 per cent of the estimated cost of Rs. 15,000 crore
The State is to fund the project entirely, with no Central role
The project is funded only through Finance Commission disaster grants
accepted.x: Under its national project status, the Centre is to fund Polavaram. An older cited estimate placed the cost at Rs. 55,548 crore, although releases have been delayed.
accepted.tq: Link statutory status with the corresponding funding responsibility and cost figure.
accepted.sec: Polavaram funding - national project status, cost reimbursement

accepted.s: The budgetary provision for Polavaram was Rs. 6,705 crore in 2025-26 and Rs. 6,105 crore in 2026-27. Which statement follows from these figures?
o: The 2026-27 provision was double the 2025-26 provision
The provision declined by Rs. 600 crore in 2026-27
The provision increased by Rs. 600 crore in 2026-27
accepted.x: The provision declined from Rs. 6,705 crore in 2025-26 to Rs. 6,105 crore in 2026-27, a decrease of Rs. 600 crore.
accepted.tq: Subtract the two year-wise provisions and identify the direction of change.
accepted.sec: Polavaram funding - national project status, cost reimbursement

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the arrangement extended to Andhra Pradesh in lieu of Special Category Status?
o: Special Category Status was granted with 90:10 CSS funding
A Special Assistance Measure of Rs. 24,350 crore was provided instead
The State was excluded from all externally aided projects
Only disaster grants were provided in place of Special Category Status
accepted.x: Special Category Status was not granted to Andhra Pradesh. Instead, a Special Assistance Measure amounting to Rs. 24,350 crore was provided.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the status demanded and the alternative assistance actually provided.
accepted.sec: Externally aided project support in lieu of Special Category Status

accepted.s: Under the package provided to Andhra Pradesh, what share of the cost of externally aided projects is borne by the Centre?
accepted.x: The Centre bears 40 per cent of the cost of externally aided projects under the package.
accepted.tq: Do not substitute the 90:10 CSS pattern for the distinct EAP cost-sharing provision.
accepted.sec: Externally aided project support in lieu of Special Category Status

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the externally aided project inflows mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Rs. 16,252 crore in 2024-25 RE and Rs. 21,585 crore in 2025-26 RE
Rs. 21,585 crore in 2024-25 RE and Rs. 16,252 crore in 2025-26 RE
Rs. 15,000 crore in 2024-25 RE and Rs. 24,350 crore in 2025-26 RE
Rs. 8,432 crore in 2024-25 RE and Rs. 5,037 crore in 2025-26 RE
accepted.x: EAP inflows were Rs. 16,252 crore in 2024-25 RE and Rs. 21,585 crore in 2025-26 RE. Almost all of the 2024-25 RE amount, Rs. 16,244 crore, consisted of loans.
accepted.tq: Match both annual values in sequence and distinguish EAP from other central-transfer categories.
accepted.sec: Externally aided project support in lieu of Special Category Status

accepted.s: In relation to Amaravati, the special central assistance that was fast-tracked was:
accepted.x: Special central assistance of Rs. 15,000 crore for Amaravati was fast-tracked.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Amaravati assistance from the wider Special Assistance Measure and the Polavaram provisions.
accepted.sec: Externally aided project support in lieu of Special Category Status

accepted.s: Which benefit is associated with Special Category Status in the context of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: 100 per cent State funding for all CSS
No matching contribution by either government
60 per cent Central funding instead of 90 per cent
90 per cent Central funding instead of 60 per cent
accepted.x: Special Category Status traditionally enabled 90 per cent Central funding for CSS, compared with 60 per cent for general States.
accepted.tq: Compare the two Centre-sharing ratios and identify the advantage attached to the status.
accepted.sec: Externally aided project support in lieu of Special Category Status

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Fourteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: It retained a separate devolution formula exclusively for Special Category States
It did not distinguish Special and General Category States in its devolution formula
It introduced Special Category Status in 1969
It restored the 90:10 CSS funding pattern for all States
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission did not distinguish Special Category and General Category States in its devolution formula. Some accounts also associate it with recommending the abolition of Special Category Status.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between devolution treatment and CSS funding benefits.
accepted.sec: Externally aided project support in lieu of Special Category Status
